name: AT&T
holdings: Holds about 314-375 MHz of sub-6 GHz spectrum across 600/700/850 MHz, PCS, AWS, WCS, C-band and 3.45 GHz, plus mmWave. In July 2026 it closed a $23B purchase of EchoStar's 30 MHz of 3.45 GHz and 20 MHz of 600 MHz, which lifted its FCC licenses to $149.4B at book on September 30, 2026.
benefits_if: Scarce spectrum limits what rivals can add and supports pricing. AT&T now owns the 3.45 GHz it used to lease, so it needs to buy less in a tight market. Higher private-deal prices also support its credit.
loses_if: Auction 115 (160 MHz of upper C-band, bidding from April 2027) and later auctions add supply and cap what its licenses would fetch. A SpaceX network on its own spectrum would add a fourth rival. AT&T fell 9.8% on October 9, 2026, the day after SpaceX agreed to buy 800 MHz.
risks: Net debt was $149.8B after the EchoStar deal. Cable and SpaceX add price competition. Book value turns into cash only through a sale, and carriers rarely sell. The shares are down about 10% over the past year.
scenario_view: Gains most if spectrum gets scarcer and holders capture it, holds up as a dividend stock if values stay steady, gives up some asset value under abundance, and does worst if SpaceX and satellite owners become a fourth force.
spectrum_basis: ~49% (license book value vs EV at late-October prices)

name: Verizon
holdings: Holds about 279-290 MHz of sub-6 GHz spectrum, led by about 161 MHz of C-band, plus 700/850 MHz, PCS/AWS, CBRS and mmWave. In 2026 it won about $3.2B of AWS-3 in Auction 113 and bought $1.0B of Array spectrum. Its licenses were about $161B at book on September 30, 2026.
benefits_if: Its deep C-band position gains value as traffic grows and new mid-band stays scarce. It hosts the Comcast and Charter mobile services on its network, so scarcity lets it charge them more.
loses_if: Auction 115 and SpaceX's spectrum add supply and a new rival. Verizon fell 8.8% on October 9, 2026. It already trades price for growth: postpaid ARPA fell 1.9% in Q3 2026 while phone net adds rose to 406,000.
risks: The market is promotional, and management has pulled back from price rises. Leverage stays high, and 2026 capex runs $16.0-16.5B. The cable services it hosts also compete with it for customers.
scenario_view: Gains most if spectrum gets scarcer and holders capture it, holds up as a dividend stock if values stay steady, gives up some asset value under abundance, and does worst if SpaceX and satellite owners become a fourth force.
spectrum_basis: ~50% (license book value vs EV at late-October prices; 52% on unsecured net debt only)

name: T-Mobile US
holdings: Holds the most sub-6 GHz spectrum of the three, about 376 MHz, built on 2.5 GHz from Sprint plus 600 MHz, PCS/AWS, C-band and 3.45 GHz. It sold its 800 MHz to Grain in August 2026 for $2.9B cash and $690M of 600 MHz licenses, and keeps half of Grain's gains above a set return. Its licenses were $100.0B at book on September 30, 2026.
benefits_if: Its mid-band lead becomes more valuable as traffic grows. It shares in the markup when Grain resells the 800 MHz to SpaceX for a reported ~$8B. It is the one carrier still raising prices: postpaid ARPA rose 4% in Q3 2026.
loses_if: SpaceX, its partner for T-Satellite, is building a rival network on its own spectrum and has sought access to 80,000 US cell sites. T-Mobile fell 13.3% on October 9, 2026, its worst day as a public company, and hit a 52-week low of $143.75 on October 28.
risks: Postpaid account adds fell 31% and account churn rose to 1.09% in Q3 2026, and it no longer reports phone net adds. Its satellite partnership with SpaceX may not survive the rivalry. It sits closest of the three to the FCC's 385 MHz spectrum-screen trigger, which limits further buying.
scenario_view: Gains if spectrum gets scarcer and holders capture it, holds up if values stay steady, gives up some asset value under abundance, and is the most exposed carrier if SpaceX and satellite owners become a fourth force.
spectrum_basis: ~41% (license book value vs EV at late-October prices)

name: EchoStar
holdings: Sold or agreed to sell its main spectrum for about $43B at deal values. It received about $20.25B in cash from AT&T, and it gets $8.5B in cash plus 261.8M SpaceX shares when the SpaceX sale closes, expected around November 2027. It still holds 700 MHz, paired AWS-3, CBRS, C-band and mmWave licenses carried at $8.45B, which it plans to sell by September 2028.
benefits_if: Its remaining licenses sell well. Auction 113 cleared AWS-3 at about $2.53/MHz-pop, which supports the value of its paired AWS-3. If SpaceX gains, so do EchoStar's 261.8M SpaceX shares.
loses_if: SPCX falls, and EchoStar carries the price risk on its SpaceX shares. Abundant supply would cut what its remaining licenses fetch before the 2028 sale deadline. The SpaceX closing could also slip or fail.
risks: At $28.6B the stock sits about 40% below a gross look-through value near $49B. That value counts 261.8M SpaceX shares at the $139.11 close on November 13, $8.5B of SpaceX cash still to come and $13.4B of cash, less about $9.7B of debt, all before taxes and wind-down costs. SpaceX's main lockup ends December 8, 2026. Two subsidiaries filed for bankruptcy in June 2026, and the Ergen family controls the company.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity through its remaining licenses, holds steady as a SpaceX holding company if values stay flat, loses some residual value under abundance, and does best if SpaceX becomes a fourth force, since most of its value is SpaceX stock.
spectrum_basis: ~34% on remaining licenses at book ($8.45B vs ~$25B EV, calc.); the rest of its value is SpaceX shares and cash

name: Anterix
holdings: Holds 900 MHz broadband licenses across most of the US. The FCC widened the band from 6 MHz to 10 MHz on February 18, 2026. Anterix sells county licenses to utilities for private LTE networks.
benefits_if: Low-band spectrum is the scarcest input. After the FCC expansion, Anterix raised its own estimate of its spectrum value to $2.5B-$7B+. A carrier, SpaceX or a utility group could buy the company or its licenses.
loses_if: Utilities adopt slowly and no large buyer appears. More low-band supply or shared spectrum weakens the case for paying up for a narrow 900 MHz block.
risks: Trailing revenue is only about $7M. Sales so far are small: CPS Energy paid $13.0M, after a discount, for Bexar County. The stock has quadrupled over the past year, so the market may already price much of the value case. Trading is thin.
scenario_view: Gains most under scarcity, most likely through a sale, holds value in a steady market as utility sales continue, loses under abundance, and could gain if SpaceX or satellite owners go after low-band, though the pool of buyers stays small.
spectrum_basis: ~95% (rough; the licenses are nearly the whole business)

name: NextNav
holdings: Holds lower 900 MHz (902-928 MHz) location licenses, about 8 MHz. It has asked the FCC to reconfigure the band for 5G positioning and broadband, and a draft FCC proposal was under White House review in March 2026.
benefits_if: An FCC grant would turn its licenses into saleable low-band spectrum while buyers are paying up for low-band. In October 2026 SpaceX urged the FCC to include lower 900 MHz in its satellite-to-phone rules, and the stock rose 12% that day.
loses_if: The FCC rejects or delays the petition. Unlicensed users and utilities oppose it, and a House appropriations rider against it has been proposed. Abundant supply elsewhere also lowers the value of a narrow band.
risks: The regulatory outcome is binary. The stock was down 32% for 2026 by late October, and the company reported Q3 2026 results on November 10. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity only if the FCC approves its plan, drifts in a steady market, loses under abundance, and could gain if SpaceX wants the band for satellite-to-phone service.

name: Array Digital Infrastructure
holdings: The former UScellular kept its spectrum and towers after selling its wireless business to T-Mobile. It closed spectrum sales to AT&T ($1.018B, January 2026) and Verizon (about $1.0B, June 2026), plus smaller sales to T-Mobile, and keeps its C-band, CBRS and mmWave licenses.
benefits_if: Its retained C-band could sell at mid-band prices to a carrier or SpaceX. Management is under no pressure to sell, so it can wait for a better bid.
loses_if: Auction 115 offers 160 MHz of upper C-band from 2027 to the same few buyers that would want Array's C-band. Its mmWave licenses have already been written down by $136.2M and then $47.7M.
risks: TDS controls it, and the free float is small. Tower revenue depends on a few carrier tenants. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity if it sells its C-band, holds as a tower company in a steady market, loses license value under abundance, and could gain if SpaceX leases its towers or buys its spectrum.

name: Telephone and Data Systems
holdings: Owns a controlling stake in Array (about 83% on pre-2026 data), so it holds Array's spectrum and towers on a look-through basis. It also runs TDS Telecom, a fiber and cable business.
benefits_if: Cash from Array's spectrum sales flows up to TDS. Higher prices for Array's C-band would add to that.
loses_if: Array gets weak bids for its remaining licenses, or fiber spending absorbs the proceeds.
risks: Its shares trade at a holding-company discount. The fiber build needs capital. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains a little under scarcity through Array, holds as a fiber company in a steady market, loses some look-through value under abundance, and sees little direct effect if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.

name: AST SpaceMobile
holdings: Has rights to up to 45 MHz of Ligado's L-band in North America (about $550M plus at least $80M a year, pending FCC approval) and bought 60 MHz of global S-band priority rights for $64.5M. It also uses partner carriers' low-band, including AT&T's and Verizon's.
spectrum_pct_ev: ~3% at the cost of its rights
benefits_if: Satellite-to-phone spectrum gets scarce, and its L-band and S-band rights gain value. Carriers that do not want to depend on SpaceX choose AST as a neutral partner.
loses_if: SpaceX's own spectrum and scale win the carrier deals. FCC rules that let satellites reuse carrier spectrum lower the value of separate satellite bands.
risks: It has 12 BlueBirds in orbit, and its 45-satellite target has slipped to mid-2027. Q3 2026 revenue was $42.3M against a market value near $25B. Inmarsat disputes its L-band rights outside North America. Shares were down about 55% in 2026 as of November 13. Launch delays and dilution remain risks.
scenario_view: Gains if satellite spectrum gets scarcer, trades on execution in a steady market, loses some edge under abundance, and gets squeezed if SpaceX becomes the dominant fourth force.
spectrum_basis: ~3% at the cost of its rights (rough); the market-implied share is higher

name: Globalstar
holdings: Holds about 25 MHz of globally harmonized satellite spectrum in L-band and S-band, with terrestrial Band 53 rights. Apple owns 20% and uses 85% of network capacity. Amazon agreed in April 2026 to buy it for $90 a share, about $11.6B, and the FCC approved the deal on October 27, 2026, with closing expected in 2027.
benefits_if: Little more upside. Holders get $90 in cash or Amazon stock capped at $90 a share, with cash limited to 40% of shares. Scarcer spectrum mostly confirms the price Amazon already agreed to pay.
loses_if: The deal fails before closing. The stock would then trade on its own spectrum value and the Apple contract.
risks: Closing risk runs until 2027. The stock portion depends on Amazon's share price. Apple holds control rights. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Stays close to the $90 deal price in all four futures, and scarcity or a SpaceX fourth force matter mainly if the deal breaks.
spectrum_basis: Spectrum is most of the $90-a-share Amazon deal value (very rough; Amazon is paying about 40x 2026 sales), but holders receive a fixed price, so spectrum prices matter only if the deal breaks.

name: Iridium
holdings: Runs a network of about 66 satellites on about 8.7 MHz of global L-band (approximate, not re-verified). Rocket Lab agreed in June 2026 to buy it for $54 a share, $27 in cash plus Rocket Lab stock under a collar, for an enterprise value of about $8.0B. Closing is expected in mid-2027.
benefits_if: Little more upside, because the deal sets the price. Demand for L-band IoT and narrowband satellite-to-phone service supports the deal. NTN Direct goes commercial with Deutsche Telekom IoT in Q4 2026.
loses_if: The deal breaks, and Starlink's direct-to-cell service then competes with its narrowband business head on.
risks: Half the price is Rocket Lab stock, so the payout moves with Rocket Lab's shares. The stock closed at $43.79 on October 23, 2026, well below the $54 headline. Shareholders approved the sale on September 24, but there was no FCC decision as of early November. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Follows the Rocket Lab deal in all four futures, spectrum scarcity matters little, and a SpaceX fourth force matters mainly if the deal fails.

name: Viasat
holdings: Owns Inmarsat's global L-band satellite spectrum and an EU 2 GHz satellite license (2x15 MHz, expiring 2027, not re-verified), plus Ka-band broadband capacity. Through Inmarsat it disputes AST's use of Ligado L-band outside North America, and it receives $535M of AST's $550M payment to Ligado.
benefits_if: Satellite-to-phone demand makes its L-band and S-band rights worth more, through a sale, a lease or a direct-to-device venture.
loses_if: Starlink's pricing erodes its broadband and aviation business. Sharing rules in the US and EU add satellite capacity in other bands.
risks: Leverage is high. Its EU 2 GHz license comes up for renewal in 2027. It faces satellite failures and competition from Starlink and Amazon Leo.
scenario_view: Gains if satellite spectrum gets scarcer, holds in a steady market, loses some value under abundance, and faces more pressure if SpaceX and Amazon dominate satellite-to-phone service.

name: SpaceX
holdings: Has agreed to buy about 79 MHz of US spectrum usable on the ground. That includes EchoStar's AWS-4 (40 MHz), H-block (10 MHz) and unpaired AWS-3 (15 MHz) for about $19.6B, closing around November 2027, and Grain's 800 MHz (up to 14 MHz) for a reported ~$8B, which the FCC is reviewing. It also runs Starlink and about 650 first-generation direct-to-cell satellites.
benefits_if: Owned spectrum lets it sell mobile service on its own network. Scarcity raises the value of spectrum it bought at about $1.0/MHz-pop for AWS-4 and H-block.
loses_if: The FCC blocks or attaches conditions to more purchases, or abundant supply lets rivals match its coverage cheaply. Carriers refuse it wholesale access, and T-Mobile has ruled that out.
risks: Spectrum is too small a share of value to drive the stock. AI costs, Starlink and launch do. The 180-day lockup ends December 8, 2026, and a 1.3B-share release on October 22 cut the stock 9% in a day. Shares have traded between about $108 and $192.50 since the June listing.
scenario_view: Gains a little under scarcity, tracks Starlink and AI in a steady market, loses a little under abundance, and gains most if it becomes a fourth force, though spectrum stays a small part of its value.
spectrum_basis: ~1.5% (about $27.6B of agreed spectrum deals against about $1.85T)
market_note: market cap $1.85T (2 Nov 2026); return +3% since $135 IPO (to 13 Nov 2026)

name: Alphabet
holdings: Holds no material licensed mobile spectrum. It owns about 5-6% of SpaceX, a stake it valued at $94.1B on June 30, 2026.
benefits_if: SPCX rises if SpaceX's spectrum and mobile plans pay off, which lifts the value of Alphabet's stake.
loses_if: SPCX falls, though the effect on Alphabet is small.
risks: The SpaceX stake is a small part of Alphabet's value. The exact stake size is uncertain after SpaceX's merger with xAI. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Barely moves in any of the four futures, and gains a little if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.

name: ERShares Private-Public Crossover ETF
holdings: An ETF that mixes listed growth stocks with stakes in private companies, including a SpaceX position (weight not verified).
benefits_if: SPCX rises as SpaceX's mobile plans pay off.
loses_if: SPCX falls. Now that SPCX trades directly, investors have less reason to pay fund fees for access.
risks: Holdings and the SpaceX weight were not verified. Exposure to spectrum is very diluted.
scenario_view: Moves little in any of the four futures and gains slightly if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.
spectrum_basis: Low (via SpaceX, where spectrum is about 1.5% of value)

name: Destiny Tech100
holdings: A listed closed-end fund that holds stakes in private and recently listed tech companies, including SpaceX (weight not verified).
benefits_if: SPCX rises as SpaceX's mobile plans pay off.
loses_if: SPCX falls, or the fund's premium to net asset value shrinks now that SPCX trades directly.
risks: The fund can trade far from net asset value. Holdings and the SpaceX weight were not verified.
scenario_view: Moves little in any of the four futures, gains slightly if SpaceX becomes a fourth force, and depends mostly on its premium to net asset value.
spectrum_basis: Low (via SpaceX, where spectrum is about 1.5% of value)

name: Comcast
holdings: Holds 10 MHz of 600 MHz in 72 areas, leased to T-Mobile under a sale worth up to $3.3B. Only $46M of that sale has closed, and the rest is targeted for the first half of 2028. It also holds 830 CBRS licenses bought for about $458M, and Xfinity Mobile, with about 10.6M lines, runs mostly on Verizon's network.
benefits_if: Higher low-band prices support its 600 MHz sale to T-Mobile, priced at about $2.21/MHz-pop if fully completed.
loses_if: Scarcity raises the wholesale rates it pays Verizon. A SpaceX mobile service adds another low-price rival.
risks: Comcast lost 144,000 broadband customers in Q3 2026. About half its Q3 postpaid mobile connects were free lines.
scenario_view: Gains a little under scarcity through its 600 MHz sale, holds in a steady market, gains slightly under abundance as wholesale costs fall, and faces another price rival if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.

name: Charter Communications
holdings: Holds 210 CBRS licenses in 106 counties, bought for $464M, which must be in use by 2030. Spectrum Mobile, now 13.5M lines including Cox, runs mostly on Verizon's network.
benefits_if: It gains little directly. It can move more traffic onto its own CBRS licenses as wholesale costs rise.
loses_if: Wholesale costs rise, and fixed wireless and satellite take broadband customers.
risks: Leverage is high. Charter lost 233,000 broadband customers in Q3 2026. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Pays more under scarcity, holds in a steady market, gains slightly under abundance as wholesale costs fall, and faces another price rival if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.

name: American Tower
holdings: Holds no licensed spectrum. It leases tower sites to carriers, so it gains when carriers need more sites to carry traffic on the spectrum they have.
benefits_if: Scarce spectrum pushes carriers to add sites. A SpaceX ground network would also need many sites. Bloomberg reported SpaceX is seeking at least 80,000 US sites, and Morgan Stanley called the Grain deal constructive for tower companies.
loses_if: Abundant spectrum and satellite coverage reduce the need for new sites, mainly in rural areas. Carrier consolidation removes tenants.
risks: It is sensitive to interest rates. It lost leases when the Dish 5G network shut down, and the FCC required a $2.4B escrow tied to tower-company litigation. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity as carriers add sites, holds in a steady market, loses some demand under abundance, and gains if SpaceX builds a ground network on leased towers.

name: Crown Castle
holdings: Holds no licensed spectrum. It owns US towers, and Bloomberg reported that SpaceX held talks with it about site access.
benefits_if: Scarce spectrum pushes carriers to add sites. A SpaceX ground network would need tens of thousands of leased sites.
loses_if: Abundant spectrum and satellite coverage reduce the need for new sites. Carrier consolidation removes tenants.
risks: It lost leases when the Dish 5G network shut down. It is sensitive to interest rates. A SpaceX lease has not been signed. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity as carriers add sites, holds in a steady market, loses some demand under abundance, and gains most of the tower group if SpaceX builds a ground network on its sites.

name: SBA Communications
holdings: Holds no licensed spectrum. It owns towers in the US and abroad and leases space on them to carriers.
benefits_if: Scarce spectrum pushes carriers to add sites, and a SpaceX ground network would need leased towers.
loses_if: Abundant spectrum and satellite coverage reduce the need for new sites. Carrier consolidation removes tenants.
risks: Leverage is high. It lost leases when Dish and EchoStar shut their network. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity as carriers add sites, holds in a steady market, loses some demand under abundance, and gains if SpaceX builds a ground network on leased towers.

name: iShares US Telecommunications ETF
holdings: A cap-weighted fund of US telecom stocks, led by the large carriers, with some small spectrum names (holdings not verified).
benefits_if: Carriers keep pricing power as spectrum gets scarcer.
loses_if: A price war, or a SpaceX fourth network, hits its largest holdings.
risks: It is concentrated in a few carriers. Holdings and weights were not verified.
scenario_view: Gains if spectrum gets scarcer and holders capture it, holds in a steady market, loses some value under abundance, and does worst if SpaceX becomes a fourth force.
spectrum_basis: Indirect (its largest carrier holdings carry ~41-50% of EV in spectrum at book)

name: SPDR S&P Telecom ETF
holdings: An equal-weight fund of US telecom stocks, which gives small spectrum and satellite names more weight than a cap-weighted fund does (holdings not verified).
benefits_if: Small spectrum names get bought at a premium, and carriers keep pricing power.
loses_if: Equipment makers in the fund hit a downturn, or carriers lose pricing power.
risks: It includes equipment makers with little spectrum exposure. Holdings were not verified.
scenario_view: Gains under scarcity through takeovers of small holders, holds in a steady market, loses some value under abundance, and is mixed if SpaceX becomes a fourth force, since it holds both carriers and satellite names.
spectrum_basis: Indirect (equal weight adds small spectrum holders)

name: Vanguard Communication Services ETF
holdings: A broad communication services fund dominated by internet and media giants. Carriers are a minority weight.
benefits_if: It gains little from spectrum prices, which reach it only through its carrier holdings.
loses_if: Its carrier holdings lose pricing power, which has a small effect on the fund.
risks: It is not a spectrum vehicle. Returns depend mostly on internet and media stocks.
scenario_view: Barely moves in any of the four futures.

name: First Trust Indxx NextG ETF
holdings: A fund of 5G and next-generation network companies, including equipment makers, chip firms and carriers (holdings not verified).
benefits_if: Scarce spectrum pushes carriers to spend more on network equipment.
loses_if: Carriers cut network spending after the 5G peak.
risks: Exposure to spectrum is very diluted. Holdings were not verified.
scenario_view: Gains a little under scarcity through equipment demand, holds in a steady market, and moves little under abundance or a SpaceX fourth force.

name: Procure Space ETF
holdings: A fund of space companies, including satellite operators (holdings not verified).
benefits_if: Satellite spectrum is revalued as buyers like Amazon and SpaceX pay up for it.
loses_if: Space stocks lose favor, or held satellite names are bought out at fixed prices.
risks: The fund is small. Holdings were not verified. Globalstar and Iridium, if held, are capped by their deal prices.
scenario_view: Gains a little under scarcity, holds in a steady market, and gains if satellite owners become a fourth force, depending on what it holds.

name: ARK Space and Defense Innovation ETF
holdings: An actively managed fund of space and defense companies (holdings not verified).
benefits_if: Satellite names it holds gain as satellite spectrum is revalued.
loses_if: Space and defense stocks lose favor.
risks: It is an active, thematic fund. Holdings were not verified.
scenario_view: Moves little with spectrum prices and gains slightly if satellite owners become a fourth force.

name: Rogers Communications
holdings: Was the biggest bidder in Canada's 2021 3500 MHz auction, paying about C$3.3B (C$3.38/MHz-pop). It paid C$475M (C$0.32/MHz-pop) in the 2023 3800 MHz auction and also holds 600 MHz and AWS. Canadian licences have little link to US prices.
benefits_if: Canadian spectrum stays scarce and supports a three-carrier market. US prices matter only as a benchmark.
loses_if: Canada's regulator pushes more competition, and new supply clears cheaply. The 3800 MHz auction priced about 90% below 3500 MHz.
risks: Leverage is high. It faces regulatory price pressure and possible satellite entry. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Feels US spectrum futures mostly at a distance, gains if Canadian spectrum stays scarce, holds in a steady market, loses if new supply clears cheaply as in 2023, and faces its own satellite competition if a SpaceX-style entrant reaches Canada.

name: Telus
holdings: Paid about C$1.9B in Canada's 2021 3500 MHz auction and about C$0.24/MHz-pop in the 2023 3800 MHz auction. It also holds 600 MHz and AWS. Canadian licences have little link to US prices.
benefits_if: Canadian spectrum stays scarce and supports a three-carrier market.
loses_if: Canada's regulator pushes more competition, and new supply clears cheaply, as 3800 MHz did in 2023.
risks: Leverage is high, and dividend cover is a concern. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Feels US spectrum futures mostly at a distance, gains if Canadian spectrum stays scarce, holds in a steady market, loses if new supply clears cheaply, and faces its own satellite competition if a SpaceX-style entrant reaches Canada.

name: BCE
holdings: Bell paid about C$2.1B in Canada's 2021 3500 MHz auction. It also holds 600 MHz and AWS. Canadian licences have little link to US prices.
benefits_if: Canadian spectrum stays scarce and supports a three-carrier market.
loses_if: Canada's regulator pushes more competition, and new supply clears cheaply, as 3800 MHz did in 2023.
risks: Leverage is high, and it is spending on US fiber expansion. November 2026 market value was not confirmed.
scenario_view: Feels US spectrum futures mostly at a distance, gains if Canadian spectrum stays scarce, holds in a steady market, loses if new supply clears cheaply, and faces its own satellite competition if a SpaceX-style entrant reaches Canada.
